threads.thread_goal: Align on current procedures and confirm scope of the integrated support programme.

messages.text: Hi team, let's kick off the Integrated Early Support Programme. To start, could everyone briefly share how their teams currently identify and refer at-risk children? This will help us map everything out for T1 and build the Current Procedures Mapping Document (A1).

Great start. On the school side, it's usually an informal observation by the teaching assistant, followed by a chat with the class teacher. If concerns persist, we log it and might raise it at a staff meeting. Formal referrals are less common unless there's a clear safeguarding issue.

From the community social work side, referrals typically come to us from multiple sources, including schools, but often after a significant event. We have a formal intake process, but the initial information from schools can be quite varied. Mapping this out in A1 will be key to finding the gaps.
We talk to the parents if we are worried about a child.

Thanks everyone. It sounds like a major gap is the lack of a shared, early-stage process before it becomes a significant event. That's exactly what this programme aims to fix. The different levels of formality are a key insight for A1.
I agree, it's mostly informal. Sometimes we just hope things get better on their own if it's not a big issue.

Exactly. To make sure we're focused, we should also define the scope of the pilot. The draft Pilot Plan (A7) suggests two classes. Does that feel right to everyone? It would give us a manageable group to test the new procedures.

Two classes sounds good from my side. We should probably focus on cases where concerns are emerging, rather than existing, complex cases. That will let us test the 'early' identification part properly.
Good point. Let's define the scope as 'emerging learning, wellbeing, or social concerns'. This will also help us manage expectations with teachers and families for the pilot outlined in T9.
Which two classes?
We can coordinate with school leadership on that, but likely one from lower and one from upper kindergarten to see if there are age-related differences. We'll document the final selection in A7.
So, are we agreed on the scope? Decision: The pilot will include two classes and focus on emerging learning, wellbeing, or social concerns.
Confirmed.
Yes, that's clear. Thanks for summarizing.
ok
Great. Now for the procedures mapping (T1). It seems like there's a school-side and a social-work side to capture. Who is best placed to pull that together into the A1 document?
I can take ownership of that. I have the context from both sides from my previous role. I'll set up the shared doc (A1) and reach out to each of you for the specific details I need.
Perfect. So, to confirm the second decision: Ownership for completing the current procedures mapping document (A1) is with @361403.

threads.thread_goal: Review and finalise the early identification and referral protocol and observation checklist.

messages.text: Hi all, following on from our discussion about procedures, I've drafted the Early Identification and Referral Protocol (A2) as part of T2. It's in the shared drive. Could the EYTAs in particular please review it against current school practices? I want to make sure it aligns with existing kindergarten procedures as per T11.

Thanks for sharing this so quickly. I've read through A2. The flow is logical, but I have a concern about the data sharing consent form on page 3. It feels a bit heavy for an initial conversation with a parent. Could we simplify it to a verbal consent model for the initial stages, with written consent required only if we proceed to a formal referral? This would align better with how we build trust with families.
I agree with @499701. A big form upfront could be a barrier. A two-stage consent process makes sense. The protocol should be very clear about what information is shared at each stage.

That's a great point about building trust. I can definitely adjust that. A two-stage consent process is fine as long as we're explicit about the triggers for written consent. I'll revise that section in A2.
What if the parents say no?

If parents don't consent, we can't share information, and the joint part of the process stops. We would continue with our standard in-school support. The protocol will make that clear. The only exception is a statutory safeguarding concern, which follows a different path anyway.

Also, let's look at the Classroom Observation Checklist (A3) for T3. I've put a draft version in the folder. The goal was to keep it completable in under 5 minutes. Can you all take a look and see if the indicators are clear and practical?
The checklist A3 looks great. It's simple and covers the key areas without being overwhelming. How often are we thinking it should be used?

I'd suggest it's not a routine weekly thing for all children, as that would be too much. It should be used when a concern is first noted, and then perhaps weekly for a few weeks for any child who is being actively monitored through the new protocol. Does that sound reasonable?
Yes, using it only when we have a concern is better. It will be too much work otherwise.
That frequency makes sense. It provides a good baseline and then tracks progress without creating a huge administrative burden. The indicators on A3 are relevant from a social work perspective too.
Okay, let's lock in that decision. The final version of the classroom observation checklist (A3) is agreed, to be used upon initial concern and then weekly for monitored children.
Great. I've updated the protocol A2 with the two-stage consent model. The link is unchanged. If there are no other major comments, can we approve it for the pilot?
The revised consent section in A2 is much better. I'm happy to approve this version.
Looks good to me too. Let's formalize it. Decision: The early identification and referral protocol (A2) is approved for pilot use.

threads.thread_goal: Define classroom support routines and align them with school procedures and workload.

messages.text: Hi team, I've drafted some ideas for the Standardised Classroom Support Routines (A4) as part of T6. The document lists a few practical strategies like 'visual timetables' and 'buddy system'. Are these realistic to implement without overloading staff?

Thanks for starting this. These are good, and many are already part of good practice. To avoid overload, we should frame them as a 'menu' of options that teachers can choose from, rather than a mandatory checklist for every child. We could group them into categories like 'Social & Emotional', 'Learning Support', etc.
I like the 'buddy system' idea. We use that sometimes and it works well. A 'quiet corner' is also a good one for children who get overwhelmed.

The 'menu' approach is smart. It empowers the teaching staff. From a social-emotional perspective, having options like a 'quiet corner' or 'check-in charts' are excellent for helping children with self-regulation. These all support social-emotional needs well.
Do we need to write down every time we use one of these?

Good question. I don't think so. The idea is that the chosen strategies for a specific child would be noted in their support plan, but we wouldn't log every single instance. It's about the routine, not the paperwork. This links to our feedback process in T10 - if a strategy isn't working, staff can flag it during the check-ins described in A8.

Exactly. Let's finalize the list. How about we go with these six: 1. Visual Timetable, 2. Buddy System, 3. Quiet Corner, 4. Emotion Check-in Chart, 5. Task Chunking, 6. Positive Reinforcement notes. That's a robust but manageable set.

That's a great set. I'll formalize the decision: The selected classroom support strategies are Visual Timetable, Buddy System, Quiet Corner, Emotion Check-in Chart, Task Chunking, and Positive Reinforcement notes.
Sounds good.
Now, how do we make sure staff can easily access this? A one-page guideline in our shared project folder seems best. We can link to it from the main protocol document.
Agreed. Let's make that the final decision here. The support routines will be documented as a one-page guideline (A4) stored in the shared drive and linked from the main protocol.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on family engagement approach and home visit criteria.

messages.text: Here is the draft for the family engagement script and leaflet for T4. It is in the folder as A5.

Thanks for putting this together. I've had a look at A5. The information is all there, but the tone feels a bit clinical. For example, it says 'This initiative will implement a multi-agency framework to monitor developmental indicators'. For parents, we might want something warmer, like 'We're starting a new programme where teachers and community workers team up to support your child's wellbeing'.
That's a great suggestion. Simple, clear language is essential to avoid causing anxiety for parents. We should go through the whole document and simplify the wording.
I agree. I can help with a rewrite. We need to emphasize partnership and support. I'll make some suggested edits directly in the A5 document for everyone to see.
Ok.

While we're on this topic, we also need to define the criteria for home visits as part of T5. I suggest a visit is recommended only when there are persistent concerns that can't be addressed in school, or when the family is facing significant barriers to engaging with the school.

That sounds like a sensible threshold. It keeps visits for when they are most needed. We must also be explicit about safety rules, like ensuring two staff members are present for initial visits or that a manager is always aware of the visit schedule. Standard lone working policies must apply.

Absolutely. I'll add a section on safety procedures to the T5 documentation, referencing our organisation's existing guidelines. So, the criteria are: 1. Persistent, unresolved concerns, 2. Significant barriers to school engagement, 3. Family requests a home-based meeting.
This is clear and robust. Let's confirm this decision: The criteria for home visits and the inclusion of standard safety rules are confirmed.
Okay, I've updated the script and leaflet in A5 with simpler, more supportive language. Please take a final look.
This is much better. It's clear, friendly, and focuses on helping. I approve this wording.
Looks good.
Perfect. Let's lock it in. Decision: The family engagement script and leaflet wording in A5 are approved.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in monitoring indicators, reporting template, and pilot start date.

messages.text: Hi team, I've created the draft Monitoring and Reporting Template (A6) for T8. I've also added a tab with proposed indicators for T12, such as 'number of positive interactions observed' and 'reduction in classroom incidents'. Please review and let me know your thoughts.

Thanks, this template is very clear. The indicators are a good start, but they feel quite quantitative. To capture the full picture, could we add a qualitative field? Something like a 'Key Observations/Successes' text box for staff to add brief notes. This would help us understand the 'why' behind the numbers.
I love that idea. A notes section would be invaluable for the pilot review. It gives staff a voice and helps us capture stories of impact. @361403 can we add that to A6?
Excellent suggestion. I've added a 'Qualitative Observations' field to the template A6. It's important we capture that context.
Where will this file be saved? Is it secure?
Yes, as noted in the template and in our protocol (A2), all completed templates will be stored in the secure case management system with restricted access, adhering to data protection policies.

Great. With all the materials now finalized, can we look at the Pilot Plan (A7) and set a start date? I propose we start in two weeks, on Monday the 15th. This gives us time to run the training session next week.
That timeline works. It feels realistic. So we are reconfirming the pilot scope of two classes, focusing on emerging concerns, with a start date of the 15th.
Correct. Let's make that official. Decision: The pilot scope is reconfirmed, and the start date is set for Monday 15th.

Works for me. One final check: the addition of the qualitative field in the monitoring template A6 should be reflected in our protocol A2. It's a minor clarification under the 'Monitoring' section. With that change, can we reconfirm approval of the protocol?
Good catch on consistency. Yes, I'm happy to reconfirm approval of A2 with that small addition.
Same here. Decision: The protocol (A2) is reconfirmed with the monitoring update.
